first_impression.reaction: Googled 'greece wedding packages all inclusive' because a Crete resort told us its package was 'all inclusive' and I didn't believe it. The intro says straight away that the phrase means different things and that food, drink and rooms are where packages split. That's the catch, stated up front. I jumped to the FAQ, then the comparison table, then the quote checklist. Named venues, named brochures with dates, actual room minimums and deposit terms. That's proof, not promises. My niggles are small: one 'informal marriage' I can't place legally, a couple of unnamed 'resorts', and headings that keep saying all-inclusive right after telling me none of them are.

journey.quote: Food and drink for the reception, exclusive use, guest rooms, extra hours and outside suppliers are where packages part ways, and most venues quote them separately.
journey.reaction: First paragraph tells me where the catch is. Nobody's selling me anything yet. Good start.

journey.section: What all inclusive means at a Greek wedding venue
journey.quote: None of the ten venues in this comparison sells its wedding package as all inclusive. The phrase belongs to the holiday, not the wedding.
journey.reaction: That's the answer I came for, and it's the opposite of what a sales page would say. Then it names Ikos, Grecotel and Atrium, so I can check it myself.

journey.quote: Elounda SA states that the Municipal fee for a civil wedding and the Metropolis fee for an Orthodox wedding are not in the package rate and are charged on top.
journey.reaction: A fee charged on top, named, with the venue that says so. That's the kind of line I'd otherwise only find on page 14 of a PDF.

journey.quote: The order is geography, not preference.
journey.reaction: Tells me nobody paid to be at the top. I notice that sort of thing.

You've just spent a whole section telling me none of these are sold as all inclusive, and then the heading calls them all-inclusive packages. Same with 'How to compare two all-inclusive quotes'. I know it's what I typed into Google, but it reads like the page forgot its own point.

journey.quote: Andronis, Oia, Santorini | Andronis Wedding Package | Ceremony arranged with the Mayor
journey.reaction: Every other row tells me civil, Orthodox, symbolic. This one tells me who arranges it. Is that a civil wedding? I'd have to go and work it out.

journey.quote: Abaton's terms are among the most specific in this comparison. Packages do not include accommodation and apply with a booking of at least 10 rooms for at least 2 nights, depending on guest numbers, and a reception of at least 20 guests, up to 300.
journey.reaction: Hard conditions with numbers. This is the stuff that blows a budget, and it's spelled out.

journey.quote: Euphoria Resort offers three options, Elxi, Pathos and Eros, for an informal wedding or vow renewal, with a certificate of informal marriage from the hotel.
journey.reaction: What's an 'informal marriage'? For Elounda you told me plainly that symbolic weddings aren't legally recognised in Greece. Here I get a 'certificate' from the hotel and no word on whether it means anything. That's exactly the kind of wording I'd expect to hide a catch.
Honest, but then it's not much use in a package comparison. Same with half the Four Seasons row reading 'Not published'. Fine as a lead, not something I can put in my spreadsheet.

journey.quote: On Corfu and elsewhere on the mainland, several resorts work by proposal rather than a named package, with no fixed inclusions published.
journey.reaction: Several resorts. Which ones? Everywhere else you name names, and this sits under an Athens heading talking about Corfu. Same thing later with 'One Corfu resort lists its outdoor ceremony venues as weather permitting.' Unnamed sources are where I stop trusting a page.

journey.section: How to compare two all-inclusive quotes like for like
journey.quote: Packages that look alike in a headline often split at the detail: one includes a cake for 10, another a two-tier cake, a third leaves the cake outside the set menu.
journey.reaction: Concrete example of why the headline means nothing. Going straight into my comparison sheet.

journey.quote: At Santorini Gem, an open bar package is optional, but once chosen it applies to all adults.
journey.reaction: That's a proper gotcha, pointed out plainly.

journey.quote: Santorini Gem takes a non-refundable deposit, with the rental balance due nine months before the wedding, food and drink paid 40 days before, and postponement only to the following season.
journey.reaction: Real payment terms with real dates. This is the section I'd show my fiancee.

journey.section: When all inclusive suits you and when to build your own
journey.quote: The planner question. Some venues require a wedding planner on top of the venue, so a package does not always remove that cost.
journey.reaction: A planning company admitting a package doesn't always save you the planner cost, and both routes get trade-offs. Balanced. I was waiting for the one-sided bit and it didn't come.

journey.quote: Ceremonies and fees are set locally, so check with the municipality and the Australian Embassy in Athens, including any fees, before you book.
journey.reaction: Points me to the government, not to themselves. Fine.

journey.quote: Does your travel insurance cover the wedding itself, including deposits paid to the venue?
journey.reaction: Good question I hadn't thought of. Practical, not fluffy.
Three words and it answers the question honestly. That's what an FAQ is for.

unanswered_questions: Is Euphoria Resort's 'informal marriage' legally recognised anywhere, or is it the same as a symbolic ceremony?
Is the Andronis ceremony a civil wedding?
Which Corfu and mainland resorts work by proposal, and which one lists its outdoor venues as weather permitting?
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission from any of these ten venues? (deferred business detail)
What does the Wedded Concierge consultation cost, and what do I walk away with? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: For more Greek settings beyond these ten, browse [our curated Greece wedding collection]
turn_offs_found.why: 'Curated' is a sales word, and it lands right after a line telling me the order is geography, not preference. Curated by what criteria? Mild, it's one word, but it's the only bit of the page that sounds like marketing.

turn_offs_found.quote: Euphoria Resort offers three options, Elxi, Pathos and Eros, for an informal wedding or vow renewal, with a certificate of informal marriage from the hotel.
turn_offs_found.why: A 'certificate of marriage' from a hotel sounds official. The page is careful to say Elounda's symbolic ceremonies aren't legally recognised, but says nothing here. If this is symbolic, I want it said as plainly as it was for Elounda, otherwise someone reads 'certificate' and thinks they're married.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the comparison table and the 'How to compare two quotes' checklist, to send to the Crete resort
My dad: the deposits and cancellation section and the travel insurance question

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so you can [book a Wedded Concierge consultation] with your shortlist of Greek packages in hand.
cta_reaction.why: The ask comes after the evidence, not before it, and 'confirms inclusions in writing' is exactly the promise the whole page told me to demand. That's consistent. What keeps it at maybe is the question I ask every planner: do you take a cut from the venue? That's a deferred business detail, so I'd ask it on the call rather than mark the page down for it.

top_3_changes: Euphoria Resort: say plainly whether the 'informal wedding' and its hotel certificate carry legal weight, the same way the Elounda entry says symbolic weddings are not legally recognised in Greece. Right now 'certificate of informal marriage' reads like a catch.

Name the venues behind 'several resorts work by proposal' and 'One Corfu resort lists its outdoor ceremony venues as weather permitting', or cut those lines, and move the Corfu paragraph out from under the Athens heading. Everywhere else the page names names.

Tidy two small consistency slips: the Andronis 'Ceremony types' cell should give a ceremony type like every other row, and the 'All-inclusive ... compared' and 'all-inclusive quotes' headings jar against the page's own point that none of these packages is sold as all inclusive (for example 'Greece wedding packages compared').

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and table first, hunted for catches, unnamed sources and one-sidedness
No invented brand facts; commission and consultation details placed in unanswered_questions as deferred
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (image slots, fact tags, CTA marker) ignored
Title, deferred business details and absence of prices not flagged as must-fix; no requests to explain sourcing or 'not published'

open_questions.question: The Euphoria 'informal marriage' line is the one point with a real legal-clarity risk. Can the writer add a plain legal-status line if the source supports it, or should it be flagged for VERIFY?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'greece wedding packages all inclusive' after a Crete resort called its package all inclusive, hence top relevance.
No prices on the page is by design and not penalised.
Title is person-set and deferred, so not assessed; the H2 heading comment is about body headings only.
